notes:
Summary: Spun up evaluation late 2025 to replace brittle in-house inference glue. Strong technical interest from ML infra (Director: Lina Torres) and product (Head of CX: Mateo Ruiz). Primary goal: replace current reranker + embeddings layer with lower tail latency and predictable cost for peak routing.

Key events:
- 2025-11-12: Intro call (Jordan + Lina) — outline architecture, want model routing by region, latency < 120ms p95 for chat paths.
- 2025-12-03: Demo of Redwood hosted + dedicated concept (Ravi led). Positive — liked prefix/KV cache and rollout controls.
- 2026-01-08: Security questionnaire submitted (SOC2 + KMS required); shared drive with redacted infra diagram.
- 2026-01-22: Cost model review — Pyxis procurement ran apples-to-apples pricing vs AWS SageMaker managed endpoints, factoring in existing EDP credits; finance flagged hyperscaler as cheaper for first 12 months.
- 2026-02-05: Internal re-org at Pyxis — ML infra manager who championed Redwood moved teams (lost internal champion).
- 2026-02-12: Final procurement sync (Fireflies ff_2026-02-12_8b3f). Decision: pilot with hyperscaler native endpoints to centralize billing and model ops on cloud provider control plane. Closed-lost.

Customer quotes / color: "We want to minimize moving parts in our infra and use the managed endpoint tooling the rest of infra already uses." — Lina Torres.

Technical notes / requirements we captured: latency target p95 <= 120ms for chat; throughput ~200 concurrent streams baseline; model choice flexible (open models + potential fine-tune) but must support quantized variants. Must integrate with company's AWS KMS and CloudTrail.

Win/loss analysis (from AE notes): primary loss driver = hyperscaler consolidation (billing + credits + internal ops familiarity). Secondary drivers = departure of internal champion and conservative finance view (preferred OPEX on single vendor). Security review showed Redwood could meet controls but procurement prioritized vendor consolidation.

Follow-up plan: Leave a short handover note to Lina summarizing cost/latency tradeoffs and checkpoint in 6 months after their pilot. Flag for inbound if hyperscaler pilot shows >20% cost or latency regressions.
